data.description:
## Context / Problem
Epic nonblack-brigandish-guillemot removes the repo-pinned op-cert trust file `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` and replaces it with an optional per-environment trust list held in each environment's own configuration (decision recorded in ADR 0125 by the sibling ADR task). Rebar's own MCP server must never run without its list. Today the server trusts certificates through `_opcert_trust_root` in `src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py` (own key, then keys pinned in the repo file, then the key embedded in the signature). So the trust list and its deployment must land BEFORE the sibling story that stops reading the repo file. This story adds the setting, makes verification honour it, and configures the MCP deployment with the 3 current keys in one change. Sequencing: lands after the ADR task merges; the validity-only story is implemented on this story's merged commit.

## Approach
1. Config key `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` (tuple of strings, default empty = unset). Add the field to `VerifyConfig` in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` next to `require_environment` (line 164), with `_documented(...)` text. Register its coercer in `_SECTIONS["verify"]` in `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` with the marker `# mechanism-ok: config_key verify.trusted_opcert_keys — 0dd0-cecb-3932-4c90 (ADR 0125 per-environment trust list)`, the same placement as the `verify.plan_review_engine` marker there. Add `("verify", "trusted_opcert_keys")` to `_EMPTY_ENV_FAULT_KEYS` so an empty `${VAR}` in a deployment raises instead of silently dropping the list. The coercer, new `_as_trusted_key_list` in `src/rebar/_config_coercion.py`, reuses `_as_str_tuple` (TOML array or comma-separated string, as `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` arrives) and validates each entry as `<env_id> <key-type> <base64> [comment]`: at least 3 whitespace-separated tokens and a base64 body that decodes; otherwise `ConfigError` naming the key and the entry's position.
2. Verification in `verify_opcert_record` (`src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py`, line 163): when the list is set, the trust root is the key embedded in the SSHSIG (`rebar.attest.sshsig.embedded_public_key`), used only if the pair (certificate principal, key type + base64 body) is listed. Order of checks: undecodable envelope gives `invalid`; a signature that does not verify gives `mismatch`; a wrong signed subject gives `mismatch` (existing `_opcert_subject_binding_error`); a valid, bound certificate whose pair is not listed gives the new verdict `untrusted` (verified false, reason naming the key fingerprint and the environment); a listed pair passes with trust basis `trust_list`. `verify.require_environment` still applies first (principal must equal it, else `foreign_key`). When the list is unset, behaviour is unchanged in this story. Every op-cert result gains `signing_key`, the `SHA256:` fingerprint of the embedded key, computed the way `signer_key_id` in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py` does (sha256 of the decoded key blob, unpadded base64). Keep `verify_opcert_record` under its complexity ceiling by putting the list check in a helper.
3. Vocabulary: add `untrusted` to the verdict enums of `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` and `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_status.schema.json`, add `trust_list` to `trust_basis` and a `signing_key` property in `verify_signature_result.schema.json`, and update `src/rebar/types.py` (the `trust_basis` Literal at line 395 and a `signing_key` key), the verdict lists in the `plan_review_status` docstrings of `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py`, and the embedded copies in `tests/interfaces/facades/mcp_tool_surface_golden.json`.
4. MCP health (`src/rebar/_mcp_opcert_health.py`, `opcert_signing_status`): when the list is set, `expected` is true and `matched` is whether (bound principal, signer key body) is listed; when it is unset, the existing pin-file comparison stays for now. The `/health` `opcert` field and the startup warning then report against the deployment's own list.
5. Deployment: set `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` in the `mcp` service environment of `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` and as an `-e` in `mcp_run_new` of `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` (line 393), identical values, listing exactly the 3 keys now in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`: `9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65` with `nava-opcert-prod` and `nava-opcert-prod rotated-20260907`, and `ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5` with `rebar-opcert`. Both files are in autodeploy's `MCP_PATHS`, so the merge rolls the MCP container with no manual step. Add an env_var `mechanism-ok` marker naming this epic if the mechanism ratchet requires one for the new compose entry.
6. Regenerate `docs/config-reference.md` (`python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`) and `docs/env-vars.md` (`python scripts/gen_env_registry.py`), and document the key in `docs/config.md`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `src/rebar/_config_sections.py`, `src/rebar/_config_coercion.py`
- `src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_opcert_health.py`
- `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json`, `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_status.schema.json`, `src/rebar/types.py`
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py` (docstrings)
- `tests/interfaces/facades/mcp_tool_surface_golden.json`
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`
- `docs/config.md`, `docs/config-reference.md`, `docs/env-vars.md` (generated)
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_trust_list.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py`, `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` (compose/docker-run parity)
Out of scope: removing the pin-file readers, the file, or `rebar trusted-env` (sibling stories); signing, which never consults the list.

## Testing
New `tests/unit/test_opcert_trust_list.py`, using real ed25519 keys made with `ssh-keygen` as the existing op-cert tests do:
- list set, certificate signed by a listed (principal, key): `certified`, trust basis `trust_list`, `signing_key` equals the key's `SHA256:` fingerprint;
- list set, valid certificate by an unlisted key: `untrusted`, verified false, reason names the fingerprint and environment;
- list set, listed key but a different principal than listed: `untrusted`;
- list set, tampered payload or cross-ticket replay: `mismatch`, not `untrusted`;
- list set with `verify.require_environment` naming another environment: `foreign_key`;
- list unset: an existing pinned-key certificate still verifies as before (regression);
- config: malformed entry raises `ConfigError` naming the position; empty `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` raises; a comma-separated value with 3 entries parses to 3;
- health: list set and signer listed gives `expected` and `matched` true and not degraded; signer unlisted gives degraded.
`tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` asserts the compose `mcp` env and `mcp_run_new` carry the same `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` value, that it parses through the config coercer to exactly the 3 (env_id, key body) pairs pinned in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` today, and the blue-green parity test covers the new `-e`.
Portability: pure-Python parsing and hashing; signature checks use the existing `ssh-keygen` path unchanged; no new subprocess, fd, path or permission handling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` set, a certificate signed by a listed key for its environment verifies with trust basis `trust_list`, and a valid certificate by an unlisted key gets verdict `untrusted` (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_trust_list.py -q`).
- [ ] With the list unset, existing op-cert verification is unchanged (checked: the existing op-cert test modules pass under `make verify`).
- [ ] The key is documented in `docs/config.md` and `docs/config-reference.md`, carries a `mechanism-ok` marker naming epic 0dd0-cecb-3932-4c90, and `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0.
- [ ] The compose `mcp` service and autodeploy's `mcp_run_new` set `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS` to the same value listing the 3 current keys (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py -q`).
- [ ] [non-codebase] After autodeploy rolls this change, the live MCP `/health` `opcert` field reads `expected: true`, `matched: true` and no `error`.
  provenance: environment=rebar Gerrit box i-00880b2c7f13527c5; principal=operator AWS profile frontier; privilege_posture=read-only SSM command running curl against the MCP loopback /health; instrument=aws ssm send-command + get-command-invocation — the health route is loopback-only, so no repository check can observe the deployed container.
- [ ] `make verify` is green, and the change lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
data.title: Op-cert trust list setting verify.trusted_opcert_keys, honoured by verification and set in the MCP deployment
